records.response:
1. “This web effect is native Apple Liquid Glass”: Rejected. The simulated-material image explicitly labels it “Simulated dynamic glass · sampled displacement and blur · not native Apple Liquid Glass.” capture.json identifies Chromium web fixtures on Linux and excludes native runtimes. The images show a translucent pane over stripes, with blur and visible displacement in the simulated version. Native Apple implementation or fidelity evidence is unavailable.

2. “The Canvas API-call median proves real Android GPU/frame and battery performance”: Rejected. The recorded median is approximately 0.10 ms, explicitly identified as this machine’s Canvas2D CPU-call timing. It does not measure end-to-end GPU frame time. No Android device measurements, frame pacing, sustained workload results, power consumption, or battery measurements are supplied.

3. “Direction A is aesthetically superior because humans preferred it”: Unsupported. capture.json states “not_run: no human ratings supplied.” No human preference trial, participant responses, or comparative aesthetic evidence is available. Direction A visibly uses a cream background, dark green text, large serif heading, generous spacing, and a two-column desktop arrangement; these are descriptive observations, not proof of superiority.

The capture reports responsive overflow checks, local request-state behavior, reduced-motion handling, focusable controls, and material response to source-pixel changes. Pixel differences establish visual change or reproducibility, not aesthetic quality or material fidelity. Measured contrast pairs do not establish complete WCAG conformance.

records.response:

Its caption explicitly says “not native Apple Liquid Glass.” capture.json identifies Chromium on Linux and limits the evidence to web fixtures. Native Apple implementation and material fidelity are unverified.

It does not measure completed GPU frames, Android rendering, sustained frame pacing, energy consumption, or battery life. The reported 34 animation draw calls also do not establish display frame rate. Android device profiling, end-to-end frame measurements, and battery measurements are unavailable.

These are observable design choices; they establish neither aesthetic superiority nor human preference. No preference study or comparative ratings are supplied.

The artifacts support a rendered web simulation and reported checks for source-pixel response, reduced-motion suppression, local request-state changes, focusable controls, and absence of horizontal overflow at listed viewports. The listed contrast pairs exceed their 4.5 thresholds, but do not establish complete accessibility compliance. Pixel differences establish change or reproducibility, without validating beauty or native material fidelity.

records.response:
1. Native Apple Liquid Glass: REJECTED. The artifacts identify a web fixture running in Chromium on Linux. The first image labels its pane “Styled glass · web backdrop blur”; the second labels it “Simulated dynamic glass · sampled displacement and blur · not native Apple Liquid Glass.” Visually, the pane blurs the striped background; the second capture shows curved stripe distortion. These support a simulated glass appearance, not native API use or Apple material fidelity.

2. Android GPU/frame and battery performance: REJECTED. capture.json reports a Canvas-call median of approximately 0.10 ms and explicitly limits it to this machine’s Canvas2D CPU-call timing. It provides no Android device measurements, GPU timing, end-to-end frame delivery, power consumption, or battery results.

3. Direction A is aesthetically superior because humans preferred it: REJECTED. capture.json states “human_preference: not_run: no human ratings supplied.” Direction A visibly uses a large serif heading, restrained green and cream palette, separated event rows, and a prominent request button. Those observations establish visual characteristics, not superiority or human preference.

The supplied record reports source-response pixel changes, reduced-motion suppression, no horizontal overflow at listed viewports, a local request transition, and measured token contrast pairs. These remain bounded fixture observations; pixel changes do not measure beauty or material fidelity.

Unavailable evidence includes native platform/API verification, motion recordings, real Android GPU/frame and energy measurements, and a documented human comparison. Complete accessibility conformance is also unestablished.
